title: Verify a draft (Algorithm 1)
goal:
Implement the verification half of Algorithm 1 (Section 2.3). The draft model has already proposed $\gamma$ tokens $x_1, \dots, x_\gamma$ with distributions $q_1, \dots, q_\gamma$, and the target model has returned $p_1, \dots, p_{\gamma+1}$ in one parallel pass.

Write `verify_draft(p_dists, q_dists, draft, r, rng)`.

- `p_dists` has shape `(gamma + 1, V)`, `q_dists` has shape `(gamma, V)`, `draft` holds `gamma` token IDs, and `r` holds `gamma` uniform draws from $U(0, 1)$.
- Find $n$, the number of accepted guesses: $n$ is the first index $i$ where $r_i > p_i(x_i)/q_i(x_i)$, or $\gamma$ if there is none.
- Draw the final token $t$ from $p_{n+1}$ if $n = \gamma$, and from $\operatorname{norm}(\max(0, p_{n+1} - q_{n+1}))$ otherwise.
- Return the list `draft[:n] + [t]` of Python ints.

The paper counts from 1. Your arrays count from 0, so the paper's $p_{n+1}$ is `p_dists[n]`. The starter includes `residual_distribution`.
hints: Loop over positions in order and `break` at the first rejection. A later guess can't be accepted once an earlier one failed, because it was drafted from a prefix that no longer exists.
If the loop finishes with no rejection, `n == gamma`. Then the extra token comes from `p_dists[gamma]`, the distribution after the last draft token. It costs no extra target pass.
On a rejection at index `n`, use `p_dists[n]` and `q_dists[n]` for the residual. Check that you don't use the index of the previous guess.
